title: FedRAMP 20x with Rev5
verdict: Two routes to one certification. 20x measures outcomes with Key Security Indicators; Rev5 implements a baseline of controls and takes no new applications after 11 June 2027.

rows.label: Purpose
rows.a: Shows that a cloud service meets FedRAMP’s Key Security Indicators.
rows.b: Shows that a cloud service implements a FedRAMP baseline of SP 800-53 controls.

rows.label: Its Unit
rows.a: An indicator such as KSI-IAM-ELP, one of 46 in 10 themes.
rows.b: A control such as AC-2, one of 155, 322 or 409 in a class’s baseline.

rows.label: Classes
rows.a: FedRAMP’s own gloss: Class A for pilots, Class B for low and Class C for moderate.
rows.b: Baselines for Classes B, C and D.

rows.label: What Comes Next
rows.a: The type FedRAMP builds on. Its rules bind active 20x services from 1 January 2027.
rows.b: FedRAMP says Rev5 will be retired. New applications end on 11 June 2027.

connect: Each Key Security Indicator names the SP 800-53 controls it relates to, so the two types meet in the control catalog. An indicator is not a bundle of controls: it is met by showing the outcome, not control by control.
noScore: Lensatic gives no strictness score here. The two types lead to the same FedRAMP Certification, and FedRAMP does not rank one above the other.
overlapLine: Counted from FedRAMP’s own rules file: how many of each Rev5 baseline’s controls at least one indicator names.
